extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers, incident management team members, and emergency management personnel (students in the NIMS ICS All-Hazards PIO course)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for Public Information Officers (PIOs) working in an all-hazards Incident Command System (ICS) context, covering duties, competencies, information operations, media relations, demobilization, and position qualification. Material is from a FEMA/ICS position-specific student manual used for training and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course Objective / Certification standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of this course, students will demonstrate, through activities and a Final Exam, the duties, responsibilities, and capabilities of an effective Public Information Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closed-book Final Exam: students must obtain 75% or higher to receive a certificate of completion. Pretest and Final Exam are based on Unit Enabling Objectives from Units 2–10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit Enabling Objectives (assessment basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each unit contains enabling objectives that define what students must know and be able to do (for example: describe the purpose and importance of incident information; describe PIO roles and responsibilities; list areas to assess PIO staff; describe initial incident information priorities and sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Exam questions are based on the Unit Enabling Objectives (Units 2–10); Unit 1 is not tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency model (core vs. hazard-specific competencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competency is a broad description that groups core behaviors necessary to perform a specific function. Core competencies are required of a PIO regardless of discipline; hazard-specific competencies are required for particular disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'flower' concept: center = core competencies, petals = hazard-specific competencies; both are required for full qualification. Hazard-specific competencies must be developed through additional agency or discipline training, field training, and completion of the Position Task Book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Task Books (PTBs) as qualification standard
rubrics_metrics.description: PTBs are the primary tools for observing and evaluating trainees aspiring to a new position within ICS; they document competencies, behaviors, and tasks a trainee must demonstrate to become qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful completion of all tasks in the PTB is the basis for recommending certification. Use NQS PTBs or other accepted PTBs (AHIMTA, NWCG) as referenced. During course activities, review the PTB at the Competencies level.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS Form 214 Activity Log: what to document
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS Form 214 documents significant activities worked on while on-duty and serves as both a personal reminder and official proof of actions taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the 'three A's'—Actions (taken to prevent hazardous activities), Agreements (made with supervisors or others), and Accidents (that occurred). Log details with times, who was informed, task completions, causes for later After Action Reports (AAR), and assignments for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and importance of incident information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide timely and accurate incident information to the public and news media because public concerns can influence incident management; if official information isn't available, other (likely inaccurate) sources will fill the vacuum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information must be accurate, timely, and from a trusted source. PIOs should be proactive to prevent misinformation and public/media reliance on inaccurate sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media use standard
rubrics_metrics.description: With the advent of social media, information available to the public and media via social platforms must be accurate and timely and provided from a trusted source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social media as a means of providing pertinent information to the general public and the media; monitor social channels for rumors and misinformation and correct them promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary duty of the Public Information Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIO’s primary duty is to provide strategic advice and counsel on information matters to the Incident Commander and staff, not merely to respond to satellite trucks and reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act as strategic advisor, ensuring information supports incident objectives, safety, and mission; maintain the role within the Command Staff hierarchy and coordinate messaging accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core PIO roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop current, accurate, and complete incident information; provide a central source of information for media and public; relieve IC and staff from media/public pressures; coordinate the Joint Information Center (JIC); track and dispel rumors; monitor sensitive political/social/environmental issues; inform incident personnel and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain situational awareness, escalate issues that affect safety or operations to the IC, and 'use the incident to communicate other key messages' while keeping affected individuals and organizations informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics and selection criteria for PIO staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess PIO staff for writing and speaking skills, willingness/ability to do on-camera interviews, availability (day/night), transportation, uniform status, and prior community relations/public affairs experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match assignments to personnel strengths (e.g., don’t force an inexperienced or unwilling on-camera PIO into a TV interview; consider radio). Ensure PTBs are being completed and signed to credit training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of PIO assignments and their duties — Command (single incident)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Command (single incident), duties include administrative oversight of the information function; external communications with public/media and community relations; internal communications within the Information Unit and upward reporting to the incident agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear roles for internal and external messaging, coordinate with agency officials, and ensure consistent, accurate release of incident information.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO role on Incident Complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: On an Incident Complex (multiple incidents under one IC/Unified Command), the PIO role is the same as for a single incident but the information must cover all incidents assigned to the complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide consolidated messaging, ensure consistency across incidents, and coordinate information collection across incident components.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO duties at Area Command (Unified Area Command)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Area Command the PIO consolidates gathering of information, provides multi-incident perspective ('the big picture'), ensures message consistency, and provides strategic support to PIOs assigned to individual incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize allocation of critical public information resources and support subordinate PIOs to maintain coordinated messaging across jurisdictions and incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO role in Emergency Operations Centers (EOCs) and MAC Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigned to EOCs or MAC Groups, the PIO functions primarily as a protocol manager and regional information coordinator—preparing and releasing summary information, assisting visiting media, scheduling briefings, and supporting joint agency messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide incident-management-changing information from the EOC; instead, prepare summaries and explain the EOC/MAC Group function. May coordinate VIP tours and share information with assisting agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Public Information Officer (APIO) role
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant PIO is the most likely role a field PIO will assume—supporting the primary PIO on tasks and assignments and handling delegated duties during incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train and prepare APIOs through course material and PTBs; clearly define delegated functions to ensure consistent information flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information gathering and source validation
rubrics_metrics.description: PIOs should identify potential public information sources, monitor them, and evaluate information for accuracy and validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer official upward reporting (e.g., ICS Form 209 Incident Status Summary) for larger incidents. Be cautious about relying on dispatch/radio/scanner traffic for quality information; use rumors only as indicators of public perception and verify before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial incident-stage PIO priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first stages, PIOs must quickly assess the situation, respond to immediate public/media demands, analyze incident potential, project information demands, and plan a course of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minimal setup (phones, easel chart, maps, basic supplies, radio/scanner, internet connectivity, TV/radio monitoring) may suffice for small incidents. Plan for escalation as complexity grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO Go-Kit contents and readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a pre-assembled Go-Kit stocked with supplies needed to operate for the first 72 hours without support; also keep a personal bag for out-of-area deployments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include critical information and materials, comply with agency requirements for transportation and weight limits, update kit with current federal/state laws and safety guidelines, and keep personal items ready for deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing personnel skill/experience on arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize experience levels of arriving personnel and delegate tasks accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign duties that match skill level; ensure less-experienced personnel get appropriate supervision and opportunities to document PTB competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other PIO logistical/operational considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider agency community relations, prior incident experience, normal home-base duties, home location (transportation logistics), special needs, training needs, and documentation requirements when assigning PIO staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be realistic about requested resources; consider political protocol needs (e.g., election years); confirm PTBs are signed and that personnel receive credit for training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Transition Meeting (Inbriefing) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The transition begins with a Team Transition Meeting attended by all IMT members, selected jurisdictional representatives, and the Agency Administrator or Agency Official; it is an essential meeting for sharing and receiving information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The meeting may be brief or extended; ensure full participation from PIO staff who are on IMTs. The agency should delegate authority to the IMT during this meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO duties during the Transition Meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: During transition, the PIO must determine whether the local agency or IMT will be the information authority, determine key agency/media contacts, who will handle sensitive local issues, availability of agency officials for interviews, level of community involvement, and any special documentation needs (photos/videos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet on-scene PIOs to 'take the local temperature,' determine what information can be released, and whether Assistant PIOs are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting with on-scene PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: The incoming PIO should meet on-scene PIOs to learn what is happening, what can be released, and if Assistant PIOs are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-scene PIOs are key to understanding local sentiment and operational realities; use them to identify immediate messaging opportunities and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources-of-information cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency dispatch and radios/scanners are not usually the best sources of quality information; early-stage radio reports are risky and may be misinterpreted by the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ICS Form 209 for larger incidents as the official upward reporting form approved by the Incident Commander. Monitor rumors to understand public perception but verify facts before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization authority and release control
rubrics_metrics.description: No personnel or equipment may leave the incident until authorized by the Incident Commander (facilitated through the Demobilization Unit); demobilization must be safe and cost-effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All releases and travel home must comply with National Work/Rest Guidelines; emphasis on ensuring personnel arrive home no later than 2200 hours local time (unless authorized), and resources have at least 8 consecutive hours off duty before beginning a shift or demobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vehicle and travel safety requirements for demobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: All vehicles leaving the incident require a safety inspection and correction of deficiencies prior to departure; vehicles should be washed to prevent spread of noxious weeds; commercial flyers must have ID and travel authorization and be given time to shower and dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demobilization Unit and/or Expanded Dispatch make flight arrangements unless another process is agreed upon. Provide minimum 24 hours notice for all releases where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization procedures and check-out (ICS Form 221)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel demobilizing permanently must complete an ICS Form 221 Demobilization Check-Out to facilitate return of non-expendable equipment, communications gear, vehicles, and other items and to ensure signatures and required unit clearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demobilization Unit coordinates check-outs with Communications, Ground Support, Facilities, Supply, Finance, and Documentation units; Demobilization Unit is the last stop and will collect the signed ICS Form 221.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization Unit Leader responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the Demobilization Plan with input, provide Expanded Dispatch with 'Tentative' releases and confirmations, make advance notifications to incident personnel, ensure all signatures on ICS Form 221, and monitor the demobilization process to maintain orderly and safe release of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with Resources Unit to keep the resource status board current; ensure released personnel receive briefings on method of travel, itinerary, and manifests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section chief and Command staff demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Section Chief (Planning, Operations, Logistics, Finance) and Command staff members (Incident Commander, Safety Officer, Liaison Officer) have specified responsibilities in the demobilization plan, including reviewing/approving the Demobilization Plan, identifying surplus resources, ensuring time/equipment reports are complete, and addressing safety considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Demobilization Plan approval signatures and processes; coordinate resource release priorities with geographic area and EOC as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority release guidelines (personnel and equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel release priorities include those who have worked continuously for 14 days, out-of-county personnel, assisting agency personnel as per agreements, and local personnel. Equipment priorities include critical resources, equipment staged long-term and no longer needed, rented/leased equipment, and equipment vital to other regional operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incident Commander, in concert with geographic area coordinators, establishes release priorities. Planning Section compiles tentative releases for IC approval and coordinates notification with Expanded Dispatch and GACC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance ratings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance ratings are required for trainees, outstanding performance, deficient performance, and by personal request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document performance ratings in accordance with incident documentation procedures and the Demobilization Check-Out process.
